standard.title: Properties affect material use
standard.description: Explain how characteristics and properties of materials, systems, components, tools and equipment affect their use when producing designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can describe how forces and the properties of materials affect function in a product or system (AC9TDE4K02). They can describe material properties in relation to how products work. They have not yet explained how properties determine selection across a range of materials, systems, components, tools and equipment — or compared production approaches across different scales or cultural contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how the characteristics and properties of materials, systems, components, tools and equipment affect how they are selected and used when producing designed solutions.

nodes.label: Material properties determine selection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify properties of a material and explain how those properties determine whether it is suitable for a specific designed solution
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two properties of a material and explain how each affects whether the material is appropriate for a specific purpose
nodes.typical_width: Describe the properties of multiple materials and explain how those properties determine their use in a designed solution — including household sustainability products, textiles, or structural applications; test or compare materials to determine which best matches the design requirements
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians used material science knowledge to select and prepare fibres for different environmental conditions — for example, twining techniques for string and rope suited to wet, dry, freshwater and saltwater applications
Investigate the properties of fibres and design an experiment to test which fabrics are warmest — explaining how measured properties map to real-world use decisions
Compare materials used in household sustainability products (water storage, insulation, solar panels) — explaining which properties make each material appropriate for its role

response_modes.reason: Students typically identify properties by name without connecting them to selection decisions. Multiple design contexts — each requiring a different set of properties to be matched — build the habit of reasoning from property to suitability rather than describing properties in isolation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The First Nations fibre and preparation techniques context is rich — it presents material property knowledge as a systematically developed, context-specific science, and the environmental variation (wet/dry, fresh/saltwater) makes the property-selection connection concrete and demanding.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two properties of a material
Explains how each property makes the material suitable or unsuitable for a specific purpose
nodes.hinge_reason: Material property reasoning in N1 is prerequisite for P01 (determining appropriate materials) and P03 (selecting and justifying material choices) — students who cannot reason from property to suitability will make unjustified material selections throughout production.

nodes.label: Tools, equipment and production methods affect outcomes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how the tools, equipment and techniques used in production affect the quality and characteristics of the designed solution
nodes.minimum_width: Describe how at least one tool or production technique affects the quality or characteristics of a designed solution
nodes.typical_width: Compare tools, equipment and techniques across different production contexts (factory, local enterprise, handmade); explain how production scale and methods affect cost, quality and design outcomes — including environmental and social impacts
wider: Compare tools, equipment and techniques used in factories with those used by local and regional enterprises — explaining how scale, cost and design intent differ between mass production and local craft production

Compare design and production of products in Australia and a country in Asia (e.g. Indonesia) — exploring how the availability and preferred properties of materials, and the design of public structures like shelters and housing, differ by context

Describe how systems in public places (community exercise environments, water treatment plants, waste management services) are designed to benefit community life — identifying the material and system properties that make each fit for purpose

response_modes.reason: Students tend to see production tools as neutral — any tool does the job. Comparing production across scales (factory vs handmade) and cultural contexts (Australia vs Asia) makes visible how tool choice and technique are themselves design decisions with trade-offs for quality, cost and cultural fit.

success_criteria: Describes how at least one production tool or technique affects the outcome
Identifies at least one trade-off between different production approaches
